title: THE ARROW OF TIME
subtitle: The laws can run backward. Our experience usually cannot.
thesis: Time's everyday direction is connected to the universe's special low-entropy beginning and the statistical tendency of isolated systems toward higher entropy.

second_law.heading: THE THERMODYNAMIC ARROW
second_law.body: For an isolated system, total entropy does not decrease. Heat spreads from warmer to cooler surroundings; the reverse is possible in principle, but overwhelmingly unlikely for macroscopic systems.

boltzmann.heading: ENTROPY COUNTS POSSIBILITIES
boltzmann.body: Ω is the number of microscopic configurations compatible with a macrostate. Macrostates with more compatible configurations are statistically favored.

microscopic.heading: MICROSCOPIC LAWS
microscopic.body: For many classical systems with time-independent forces, the equations are time-reversal symmetric: reversing a trajectory's velocities can produce another valid trajectory. The equations alone do not explain why entropy began so low.

cosmic.heading: THE COSMIC CLUE
cosmic.body: The early universe was extraordinarily smooth, with low gravitational entropy. How those special initial conditions arose is still a deep question in cosmology. Expansion by itself is not the complete explanation.

takeaway: The arrow of time links a special cosmic beginning with the statistics of change.
caption: Why does time seem to move forward? The Second Law says total entropy in an isolated system does not decrease: ΔS_total ≥ 0. Boltzmann's relation S = k_B ln Ω connects entropy to the number of compatible microscopic states. Yet many microscopic laws are approximately time-reversal symmetric. The puzzle is why the universe began in an extraordinarily special, low-gravitational-entropy state. The arrow of time is therefore a story about initial conditions and statistical behavior—not simply a direction written into every equation. Which part of this puzzle would you explore next?
